💡 Did you know? Serverless is the endpoint of a 20-year trend: physical servers → virtual machines → containers → serverless. At each step you manage less, until all that's left is your code and the event that triggers it.
🖥️ Did you know? "Serverless" doesn't mean there are no servers! They're still there — AWS runs them, and you simply never log in, patch, or scale them.
📝 Did you know? Serverless fits in one sentence: you don't provision, patch or scale servers, and you pay only when your code runs.
🧩 Did you know? Four traits define a serverless service: 1️⃣ No server management 2️⃣ Automatic scaling 3️⃣ Pay-per-use 4️⃣ Event-driven
🧠 Did you realize? The biggest shift in serverless isn't cost — it's the mental model. Stop thinking in processes that wait, start thinking in functions that react.
📈 Did you know? Serverless services scale from zero to thousands of concurrent executions — and back down to zero — automatically, with no capacity planning.
💸 Did you know? With serverless you're billed per request and per millisecond, never per idle hour. Idle means $0.
🧱 Did you know? Serverless ≠ Lambda! Lambda is just the compute layer. APIs (API Gateway), data (DynamoDB), storage (S3) and messaging (SQS, EventBridge) can all be serverless too.
⚖️ Did you know? Serverless is not always cheaper. It shines with spiky traffic, but a constantly busy, high, steady workload may cost less on containers.
🏭 Did you know? Serverless isn't only for small scripts — entire production backends run this way today.
😴 Did you know? Serverless means zero ops overhead: no patching, no fleet management, and no 3 a.m. disk-full pages.
🛡️ Did you know? AWS serverless services give you resilience built in: Multi-AZ by default, plus retries and dead-letter queues out of the box.
🥶 Did you know? A cold start is the extra latency on the first call after a function has been idle. Illustratively: warm ≈ 5 ms, Node.js cold ≈ 200–500 ms, Java (JVM) cold ≈ 1–2 s.
⚡ Did you know? You can shrink Lambda cold starts with smaller bundles, ARM (Graviton), and provisioned concurrency.
⏱️ Did you know? A single AWS Lambda invocation can run for at most 15 minutes. Longer jobs need a different tool.
🔒 Did you know? Serverless comes with some vendor lock-in: event shapes, IAM and integrations are AWS-specific. Know the trade-off before you commit.
🔍 Did you know? Debugging serverless can be harder: it's ephemeral and distributed, so you end up correlating many small logs across services.
⛰️ Did you know? Rule of thumb: if your traffic graph looks like mountains ⛰️, serverless wins. If it's a flat plateau ➖, run the numbers against containers.
✅ Did you know? Great fits for serverless: APIs with variable traffic, event processing (uploads, resizing, ETL), scheduled jobs, glue code between services, and prototypes/MVPs.
⚠️ Did you know? Think twice before going serverless for: jobs over 15 minutes, latency-critical paths, very high steady load, stateful work (WebSockets, in-memory caches), or GPU workloads.
💰 Did you consider? When choosing between serverless and containers, pick whichever is cheaper to operate — not just cheaper on the bill.
🚪 Did you know? API Gateway is the front door of a serverless app, providing HTTP, REST and WebSocket endpoints in front of Lambda.
🗄️ Did you know? DynamoDB is a serverless key-value and document store with single-digit millisecond latency that scales itself.
🪣 Did you know? Amazon S3 isn't just storage for objects at any scale — it's also an event source that can trigger pipelines.

🏗️ Did you know? The canonical serverless web app: static frontend on S3 + CloudFront, API Gateway routing to Lambda, DynamoDB for records, S3 for uploads, and SQS/EventBridge for async work. You can build it all without a single EC2 instance!
🔌 Did you know? A Lambda REST handler has no Express app, no port, and no listen() — the platform calls your function. Just return statusCode + body; that's the whole contract with API Gateway.
🚀 Did you know? Creating SDK clients outside the Lambda handler lets them survive across warm invocations — the single most common performance fix in Lambda code.
🖼️ Did you know? With an S3 event → Lambda trigger, the upload itself runs your code — no cron, no polling, no worker process. Thumbnail generation is the "hello world" of event-driven design.

🌙 Did you know? A nightly pipeline can be EventBridge schedule → Lambda → SQS → Lambda: fan out one message per job, run hundreds in parallel, get retries for free, and pay nothing for the other 23 hours.
🎯 Did you know? Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, S3 and SQS cover most needs. Start small: sam init → sam deploy --guided takes you from an empty account to a live endpoint in about 20 minutes!
